projects.name: M5AirQ-Rust
properties: Requests without a valid session, bearer token or API key are never granted; expired sessions and empty secrets never grant
State-changing routes require admin rights; token-over-HTTP is refused when disabled
OTA writes target the inactive slot, stay in bounds and are sequential
A failed flash write poisons the session; an update completes only if read-back, magic, CRC and activation all succeed

theorem_list.name: transition_total
theorem_list.doc: No command panics, for any actor and state.

theorem_list.name: sound
theorem_list.doc: Every accepted read-only command writes nothing, for all actors/states.

theorem_list.name: write_bounded
theorem_list.doc: A committed chunk never pushes the cursor past the declared image size.

theorem_list.name: write_sequential
theorem_list.doc: A committed chunk writes exactly at the cursor and advances it by its length: writes are strictly sequential.

theorem_list.name: end_integrity
theorem_list.doc: `end` activates a new image only when it is complete, has the ESP image magic, and matches the declared CRC.

theorem_list.name: end_failure_closes
theorem_list.doc: A failed verification (read-back, magic, CRC or activation) closes the session with the error set: the device never keeps accepting chunks into an image that failed, and never reports it as activated.

theorem_list.name: write_io_failure_poisons
theorem_list.doc: A chunk whose flash write failed is not counted: the cursor does not move and the session is poisoned (later writes are refused). Rules out a port that commits the chunk before its IO succeeded -- the divergence the Renode equivalence run found in the first version of this kernel.

theorem_list.name: begin_targets_other_slot
theorem_list.doc: `begin` never targets the running slot (it writes the inactive one).

theorem_list.name: mutating_needs_admin
theorem_list.doc: Every mutating OTA command is refused without the admin actor.

theorem_list.name: inv_reachable
theorem_list.doc: The invariant holds in every reachable state, after any sequence of commands from any actors, successful or refused.

theorem_list.name: end_accepts_any_matching_crc
theorem_list.doc: For *any* fully-written session and *any* image CRC, `end` succeeds when the declared CRC equals the (client-chosen) image CRC and the magic byte is present. The only integrity gate is a value the uploader controls: there is no signature / authenticity check (CWE-347).

theorem_list.name: check_auth_total
theorem_list.doc: `check_auth` never panics.

theorem_list.name: validate_session_sound
theorem_list.doc: If `validate_session` accepts a token then some slot accepts it.

theorem_list.name: slot_valid_fresh
theorem_list.doc: SECURITY (S): a slot accepts a token only while it is within its TTL — `slot_valid` genuinely checks `age_ok`. Kills a kernel that drops the expiry check.

theorem_list.name: unauth_never_granted
theorem_list.doc: SECURITY (S): with `public_access` off, a non-health request that carries no valid credential is never granted (refused with `Forbidden` or `Challenge`).

theorem_list.name: token_over_http_forbidden
theorem_list.doc: SECURITY (S): a bearer token or API key presented over plaintext HTTP, with token-over-HTTP disabled and no valid session cookie, is refused.

theorem_list.name: expired_session_never_grants
theorem_list.doc: SECURITY (S): an expired session cookie never grants access.

theorem_list.name: empty_secret_no_bypass
theorem_list.doc: SECURITY (S): an unset bearer token / API key never grants access, even if the (empty) comparison reported a match.

theorem_list.name: public_access_opens_everything
theorem_list.doc: FINDING (F): `public_access` (the shipped default) grants every request with no credential at all.

projects.name: SpoolEase
properties: Unauthenticated requests are refused
Every committed inventory row can be read back after a reboot
New spool ids are fresh; edits that change nothing write nothing; deleting an absent spool is a no-op
Rows stay within the store's size limits when they grow or are relocated

theorem_list.name: place_capacity
theorem_list.doc: (S) `place` never lets the file grow past the cap, and the row it places lies wholly inside the new file (given the old slot, if any, was in it).

theorem_list.name: place_local
theorem_list.doc: (S) Every byte `place` writes (its `void` and `data` regions) lies in fresh space at/after the old end of file or in the record's *own* old slot, never in another record's bytes.

theorem_list.name: place_inplace_fits
theorem_list.doc: (S) An in-place rewrite (the file does not grow) happens only when the row fits the old slot, and then it writes exactly the old slot (nothing voided).

theorem_list.name: place_grow_relocates
theorem_list.doc: (S) A row that grows past its old slot is never written in place: it is appended at the old end of file and its old slot is voided whole.

theorem_list.name: strike_relocates
theorem_list.doc: (S) When an add strikes out the spool that held its tag, the struck row (one byte longer) is appended at or past the old end of file, and the spool's whole old slot (one byte shorter than the new row) is voided: it is never rewritten in place, where it would overrun into the next record. Rules out the `strike_inplace` mutant.

theorem_list.name: fresh_id_is_new
theorem_list.doc: (S) The spool id `AddSpool` hands out is new: no record already has it. Rules out the `fresh_id_reuse` mutant (a new spool shadowing an existing record's storage). Needs only that existing ids are `≤ last_id`.

theorem_list.name: add_len_ok
theorem_list.doc: (S) An add is only accepted for a row of `1 ..= MAX_REC` bytes (one that serialises in `max_record_width`). Rules out the `add_no_len_check` mutant.

theorem_list.name: edit_same_writes_nothing
theorem_list.doc: (S) An edit that changes nothing writes nothing (`CsvDb::insert` returns early for an equal record): no region of the file is touched and it does not grow.

theorem_list.name: delete_absent_noop
theorem_list.doc: (S) Deleting a spool that does not exist changes nothing.

theorem_list.name: unauth_refused
theorem_list.doc: (S) A request that did not decrypt (`admin = false`) never mutates: every write command is refused with `Forbidden`, before any state change.

theorem_list.name: committed_rows_readable
theorem_list.doc: (S) The kernel only commits a row that the boot loader reads back: an accepted add, or an accepted edit that writes, had `readable` set. Upstream writes such rows (a note over 256 bytes or with a line break) and its whole inventory is unavailable after the next reset (found in Renode). Rules out the `unreadable_add` mutant.

theorem_list.name: sound
theorem_list.doc: Every accepted `Query` writes nothing, for all actors and states.

theorem_list.name: transition_total
theorem_list.doc: (C) `transition` never panics / overflows, for any actor, store and command (given the record and index counts fit a `usize`). A panic on the device is a reset.

theorem_list.name: addspool_id
theorem_list.doc: `AddSpool` assigns `last_id + 1`.

theorem_list.name: index_insert_spec
theorem_list.doc: `index_insert` keeps at most one more entry than it was given.

theorem_list.name: append_slot_spec
theorem_list.doc: The append loop copies every slot; the final push adds `slot`.

projects.name: td-free
properties: Spoolman requests are forwarded only to a usable server; calibration needs a client; device info needs a ready sensor
Read-only requests change no stored state; Wi-Fi updates reset the connection
Boot never locks the user out of Wi-Fi setup
Sensor register updates change only the intended bits

theorem_list.name: spoolman_forward_needs_usable_server
theorem_list.doc: (S) A Spoolman request is handed to the Spoolman client only when a server is configured with an IPv4 host and a port. Upstream hands it over with any host and the client crashes (`Ipv4Address::from_str(..).unwrap()`, found in Renode); rules out the `spoolman_any_host` mutant.

theorem_list.name: calibrate_needs_client
theorem_list.doc: (S) A calibration is started only when a client is listening for its result (upstream's 428 otherwise).

theorem_list.name: info_needs_ready
theorem_list.doc: (S) The device info is served only once the sensor task has published it; before, the request is refused (503). Upstream unwraps an empty watch and the device resets (found in Renode); rules out the `info_unguarded` mutant.

theorem_list.name: wifi_update_resets
theorem_list.doc: (S) A Wi-Fi update is stored and the device resets to use it (upstream `data_update_save_task`): the reset is always scheduled.

theorem_list.name: updates_keyed
theorem_list.doc: (S) Every update is stored under its own NVS key: settings under `SET`, RGB multipliers under `RGB`, Wi-Fi credentials under `WF_CR`; no update overwrites another kind.

theorem_list.name: reads_store_nothing
theorem_list.doc: (S) Reads store nothing: settings, RGB multipliers and device info are answered without a write set.

theorem_list.name: boot_wifi_no_lockout
theorem_list.doc: (S) Stored Wi-Fi credentials that do not work (no connection, or no address) are always forgotten and the device resets into its access point: a wrong Wi-Fi update can never lock the device out.

theorem_list.name: dev_transition_total
theorem_list.doc: (C) The HTTP decision never fails (no panic, no overflow): any request, any state.

theorem_list.name: boot_wifi_ap
theorem_list.doc: (C) Without credentials the device is an access point.

theorem_list.name: set_bits_preserves_complement
theorem_list.doc: (S) Field isolation: writing the `mask` field leaves every bit of a disjoint field `m` unchanged (mutant `set_bits_value_unmasked`).

theorem_list.name: set_bits_sets_masked
theorem_list.doc: (C) The `mask` field is set to `value` (restricted to the field).

theorem_list.name: set_gain_preserves_shutdown
theorem_list.doc: (S) Setting the gain never changes the shutdown bits (mutant `set_gain_wrong_mask`).

theorem_list.name: set_it_preserves_shutdown
theorem_list.doc: (S) Setting the integration time never changes the shutdown bits.

theorem_list.name: set_it_preserves_gain
theorem_list.doc: (S) Setting the integration time never changes the gain.

theorem_list.name: set_gain_preserves_it
theorem_list.doc: (S) Setting the gain never changes the integration time.

theorem_list.name: enable_clears_shutdown
theorem_list.doc: (S) `enable` powers the sensor on: both shutdown bits clear.

theorem_list.name: disable_sets_shutdown
theorem_list.doc: (C) `disable` sets the chip-shutdown bit.

theorem_list.name: set_bits_total
theorem_list.doc: (C) `set_bits` is total.

theorem_list.name: it_mask_collision
theorem_list.doc: (F) The integration-time encodings overflow `IT_MASK`: `IT_25MS` and `IT_50MS` set bits outside the 3-bit field, so after masking `_50ms` and `_100ms` are the same. Latent: `set_integration_time` is never called.

projects.normal_note: All 239 differing scenarios trace to one upstream behaviour on normal input: the filament list is lost when Spoolman's reply arrives during a 2 ms sleep in the handler.

projects.name: pico-bit
properties: File names cannot traverse paths and decode to confined, ASCII names
Percent-decoding and request classification are total (never fail)
Mutations need POST or DELETE; deletes never touch the payload
Uploads are bounded; the network route exposes only the staged binary

theorem_list.name: valid_name_no_traversal
theorem_list.doc: **Security (S): no path traversal.** Every filename the gate accepts is a non-empty, ≤64-byte component that is neither `.` nor `..` and contains no path separator or NUL. Appending it after `/armory/` therefore names a direct child of the armory directory: the device can never be steered to a file outside `/armory`. Falsified by `drop_slash_check` (a `/`/`\` could pass) and `drop_dotdot_check` (`..` could pass).

theorem_list.name: decode_filename_confined
theorem_list.doc: **Security (S): decode-then-validate confinement.** Even after percent-decoding, any filename `decode_filename` accepts satisfies the confinement policy on the decoded bytes. This is what makes `%2e%2e` (`..`) and `%2f` (`/`) harmless: they are decoded first and then rejected. Falsified by `validate_before_decode` (validating the raw, still-encoded bytes would accept a decoded `..`).

theorem_list.name: decode_filename_total
theorem_list.doc: `decode_filename` is total (never panics). (C)

theorem_list.name: percent_decode_total
theorem_list.doc: `percent_decode` is total (never panics), for any input and buffer. (C)

theorem_list.name: valid_name_total
theorem_list.doc: `valid_name` is total (never panics), for any slice. (C)

theorem_list.name: classify_total
theorem_list.doc: `classify` is total (never panics), for any input. (C)

theorem_list.name: dispatch_pending_goes_to_parser
theorem_list.doc: **S (U1 fix).** A preflight on which some route pattern is still open (`pending`) is never handed to a hand-written handler: it goes to the full HTTP parser. Upstream classified such a preflight by a two-way prefix match (a fragmented `POST /api/payload/run` became a payload save).

theorem_list.name: dispatch_ready_classifies
theorem_list.doc: **C.** On a decisive preflight the port runs upstream's classifier.

theorem_list.name: dispatch_total
theorem_list.doc: `dispatch` never panics. (C)

theorem_list.name: decode_filename_ascii
theorem_list.doc: **S (U5 fix).** Every byte of a name `decode_filename` accepts is ASCII, so building the LittleFS path from it cannot fail: upstream's `StorageManager::with_path` unwraps that conversion, and a DELETE of `%e2%82%ac` (a valid UTF-8, non-ASCII name) panicked the device.

theorem_list.name: mutation_needs_post_or_delete
theorem_list.doc: **S.** Whatever the port dispatches to a state-changing handler (upload, delete, payload save or run, keyboard target) came with a `POST ` or `DELETE ` method: no GET/HEAD (a link, an image tag, a prefetch) changes the device.

theorem_list.name: ncm_route_restricted
theorem_list.doc: **S.** The USB NCM worker serves nothing but the Armory listing, Armory downloads and OPTIONS: every other class is an empty 404.

theorem_list.name: ncm_exposes_only_staged_binary
theorem_list.doc: **S.** On NCM, the only file a download can return is the staged binary (`/armory/payload.bin`); `payload.dd` is portal-only.

theorem_list.name: delete_never_payload_dd
theorem_list.doc: **S.** A DELETE that the kernel lets through (`Erase`) never names `payload.dd`, the editor's file (upstream answers 403 for it).

theorem_list.name: list_entry_one_asset
theorem_list.doc: **C.** Once an asset is listed, no further one is (the listing shows at most one Armory file).

theorem_list.name: list_entry_ncm_hidden
theorem_list.doc: **S.** On NCM a file that is not the staged binary is never listed.

projects.name: anova-oven-rs
properties: Retry backoff is bounded and monotone; a successful poll recovers
User requests pre-empt polling; queue operations keep other entries
Reset classification never masks a panic; cold boot dominates
The invariant holds in every reachable state

theorem_list.name: transition_total
theorem_list.doc: No command panics, on any state.

theorem_list.name: inv_reachable
theorem_list.doc: In every reachable scheduler state — after any sequence of commands, successful or refused — the next poll is scheduled within 30 s.

theorem_list.name: enqueue_keeps_others
theorem_list.doc: Enqueuing one kind never evicts another: every other kind's pending state is unchanged. A scheduled Stop therefore survives any later poll scheduling.

theorem_list.name: enqueue_never_delays
theorem_list.doc: A `PreferEarlier` re-enqueue never *delays* a command already pending: if `k` was due at `e`, after the enqueue it is due at some time `≤ e`. So re-scheduling a Stop can only move it earlier, never later.

theorem_list.name: pop_clears
theorem_list.doc: A popped event's slot is cleared: after `pop_due` returns a kind, that kind is no longer pending, so the same scheduled event is never executed twice.

theorem_list.name: pop_keeps_others
theorem_list.doc: Popping one event leaves every other pending event pending, at its time.

theorem_list.name: ties_follow_vector_order
theorem_list.doc: Two polls due at the same instant (same priority) pop in upstream's vector order: the one at the lower index first — `soonest_index`'s `min_by` keeps the first of equal elements.

theorem_list.name: fill_hole_moves_last
theorem_list.doc: `swap_remove`'s move: a pending kind at the last index takes the freed index `p`; nothing else moves.

theorem_list.name: poll_fail_counts
theorem_list.doc: A failed poll counts one more consecutive failure (until `u64::MAX`), so `/health` and the display show upstream's count, not one capped at a tier.

theorem_list.name: user_preempts_poll
theorem_list.doc: A representative preemption: a status poll and a Stop both due at the same instant `t`, the poll first in the vector — the Stop still pops first. The `user_loses_priority` mutant (swapping the tie-break) makes this pop the poll.

theorem_list.name: poll_ok_recovers
theorem_list.doc: A single successful poll clears the failure count, so the device leaves the offline/backoff regime immediately: not offline, and polling at the 1 s rate.

theorem_list.name: backoff_bounded
theorem_list.doc: The next poll is always scheduled between 1 and 30 seconds out: the backoff is bounded, so a failing device keeps retrying and never abandons the server.

theorem_list.name: backoff_monotone
theorem_list.doc: More consecutive failures never shorten the poll interval.

theorem_list.name: panic_never_masked
theorem_list.doc: A panic is attributed to the panic even when the watchdog also fired: the root cause is never masked as a plain watchdog timeout.

theorem_list.name: coldboot_dominates
theorem_list.doc: With RAM lost (invalid magic) the boot is always a cold boot, whatever the other breadcrumbs say.

theorem_list.name: sound
theorem_list.doc: Every accepted read-only command writes nothing, for all states.

projects.name: esp-hal-wifimanager
projects.interface: HTTP captive portal: Wi-Fi provisioning + OTA
properties: Only credentials that connected are stored; invalid or superseded setups are never stored
Oversized setups are ignored; setups after connecting are refused
OTA needs its parameters; reset only after a verified image
Read-only requests change nothing

theorem_list.name: store_only_connected
theorem_list.doc: (S) A setup is stored in NVS only after it connected, and only if no newer setup was submitted meanwhile: a wrong password, an unknown network, an unparsable or rejected setup is never stored (so a bad setup can not survive a reset and keep the device off the network).

theorem_list.name: ip_only_when_connected
theorem_list.doc: (S) `/status` shows the station address only when connected.

theorem_list.name: end_only_connected
theorem_list.doc: (S) Provisioning (the open AP) ends only after a connection.

theorem_list.name: invalid_never_stored
theorem_list.doc: (S) An invalid setup (unparsable, or rejected by the driver) is reported as `failed:invalid` and never stored.

theorem_list.name: setup_starts_connecting
theorem_list.doc: (S) A submitted setup sets the status to `connecting` (the panel never reads the previous attempt's result as this one's).

theorem_list.name: oversized_setup_ignored
theorem_list.doc: (S) An oversized setup changes nothing (413).

theorem_list.name: unparsable_stored_deleted
theorem_list.doc: (S) A stored setup that does not parse is deleted (a corrupt entry can not make every boot fail).

theorem_list.name: ota_needs_params
theorem_list.doc: (S) An upload begins only with its size, CRC and length.

theorem_list.name: ota_reset_only_verified
theorem_list.doc: (S) The device resets into an uploaded image only if every write succeeded, the image is complete and it verified.

theorem_list.name: reads_change_nothing
theorem_list.doc: (S) Requests other than `/setup` and a connected `/status` change nothing.

theorem_list.name: no_attempt_without_setup
theorem_list.doc: (C) The worker reports nothing unless it is trying a setup.

theorem_list.name: superseded_not_stored
theorem_list.doc: (S) An attempt overtaken by a newer submission reports nothing, stores nothing and does not end provisioning: `/status` keeps saying `connecting` for the newer setup.

theorem_list.name: take_only_pending
theorem_list.doc: (C) The worker takes a setup only when one was submitted, and then reports `connecting`.

theorem_list.name: setup_after_connect_refused
theorem_list.doc: (S) Once a setup connected and was stored, a later setup is refused and changes nothing: it can neither replace the stored one nor keep the AP up.

theorem_list.name: connected_stays_until_end
theorem_list.doc: (L) After the connection, no request moves the status off `connected` (so `end` fires: the AP goes down).

projects.name: heater-control
properties: Duty sent to the heater is at most 100%; out-of-range duty is refused
Anonymous, mismatched or expired remotes are refused and send nothing
Over-temperature locks the heater until it cools; a missing reading locks it
SSR pulse patterns stay within 0–100%

theorem_list.name: duty_out_of_range_refused
theorem_list.doc: (S) A duty over 100 % is refused and changes nothing.

theorem_list.name: sent_duty_le_100
theorem_list.doc: (S) Whatever is sent to the SSR is the message's duty, at most 100 %.

theorem_list.name: remote_mismatch_refused
theorem_list.doc: (S) A remote that is not the one in control is refused: nothing changes, nothing is sent.

theorem_list.name: expired_remote_refused
theorem_list.doc: (S) The remote in control that missed its check-in is refused (the expiry task then takes the duty to 0).

theorem_list.name: anonymous_refused
theorem_list.doc: (S) A command without a non-blank `device` property is refused.

theorem_list.name: remote_must_check_in
theorem_list.doc: (S) A remote in control after a command expires at most 60 s after it: a remote that stops checking in loses control.

theorem_list.name: refused_sends_nothing
theorem_list.doc: (S) Only a remote's check-in or a manual command sends a duty, and only the message's: an unparsed, anonymous or refused one sends nothing.

theorem_list.name: expire_zeroes
theorem_list.doc: (S) A remote past its check-in loses control and the duty goes to 0.

theorem_list.name: expire_only_expired
theorem_list.doc: (S) The expiry touches nothing else: a live remote, manual control or no controller.

theorem_list.name: reset_only_unretained
theorem_list.doc: (S) A retained `reset` does not reset the device (no reset loop at every connection).

theorem_list.name: overtemp_locks
theorem_list.doc: (S) A valid reading at or over 70 °C locks the SSR.

theorem_list.name: locked_until_cool
theorem_list.doc: (S) A locked SSR stays locked until a valid reading under 30 °C.

theorem_list.name: invalid_reading_ignored
theorem_list.doc: (S) A reading without a temperature (a sensor error) changes nothing: in particular it does not move the deadline.

theorem_list.name: missing_locks
theorem_list.doc: (S) No valid reading by the deadline locks the SSR.

theorem_list.name: ssr_lock_zeroes
theorem_list.doc: (S) A lock zeroes the pattern.

theorem_list.name: ssr_locked_ignores_duty
theorem_list.doc: (S) While locked (and not unlocked), a duty is ignored.

theorem_list.name: ssr_pattern_le_100
theorem_list.doc: (S) The pattern's duty is never over 100 %.

theorem_list.name: pattern_zero_off
theorem_list.doc: (S) 0 % never conducts.

theorem_list.name: pattern_full_on
theorem_list.doc: (S) 100 % conducts at every step.

theorem_list.name: pattern_out_of_range_off
theorem_list.doc: (C) Outside 0..100 % or past the last step, nothing conducts (upstream panics on a duty over 100; no caller passes one).

projects.name: rc-car
properties: Motor and steering percentages stay in range for every command
Servo duty stays within the pulse range; the arithmetic cannot overflow
Brake light only on deceleration and off after its timeout
Blinker commands take effect; blinker off turns the lamps off

theorem_list.name: motor_percentage_bounded
theorem_list.doc: **S.** Whatever `MotorPower` arrives over the air (any `i32`), the ESC gets 0..=100 %. Upstream's `(value + 50) as u8` gives 255 % for -51.

theorem_list.name: motor_percentage_upstream_range
theorem_list.doc: **C.** On the controller's range -50..=50 the percentage is upstream's `value + 50`.

theorem_list.name: steering_percentage_bounded
theorem_list.doc: **S.** The steering servo gets 38..=62 % for any `SteeringPosition`.

theorem_list.name: servo_duty_within_pulse_range
theorem_list.doc: **S.** The PWM duty stays within the servo's pulse range: between the duties of `min_us` and `max_us`, for the servo's constants (`min ≤ max`, `(max - min) · 100` and `max · duty_space` fit in 32 bits, a non-zero cycle; upstream's `types.rs` constants satisfy them).

theorem_list.name: magnitude_spec
theorem_list.doc: **S.** `magnitude` is `|v|`, also for `i32::MIN` (upstream's `abs` overflows there).

theorem_list.name: brake_off_after_timeout
theorem_list.doc: **S.** A brake light on for more than 500 ms goes off at the next tick.

theorem_list.name: brake_on_only_when_slowing
theorem_list.doc: **S.** The brake light comes on exactly when the motor's magnitude drops (for every `i32`, `i32::MIN` included).

theorem_list.name: blinker_command_takes_effect
theorem_list.doc: **S (U2 fix).** While a pattern blinks, a blinker command takes effect: the new pattern is the command (upstream kept toggling the first one).

theorem_list.name: blinker_off_lamps_off
theorem_list.doc: **S.** `Off` always leaves the blinker idle with both lamps off (idle: the lamps are driven off; blinking: the command's lamps are off).

theorem_list.name: blinker_tick_alternates
theorem_list.doc: **C.** A tick flips the phase; the lamps are off in the off phase and follow the pattern in the on phase.

projects.name: crown-of-the-lamb
properties: Only valid AP names are stored; settings are clamped into range
A pending save completes before a restart
OTA is POST-only, one at a time, bounded, checks the first sector's magic
The device restarts only into a committed image

theorem_list.name: clamp_in_range
theorem_list.doc: (S) Every stored configuration value is within its field's range (the eye renderer and the colour packing rely on it).

theorem_list.name: clamp_keeps_in_range
theorem_list.doc: (S) A value already in range is stored as submitted.

theorem_list.name: expression_codes
theorem_list.doc: (S) Exactly the documented codes are taken.

theorem_list.name: wifi_refuses_bad_name
theorem_list.doc: (S) An empty AP name, or one over 32 bytes, is refused (upstream stores it as an empty name and restarts into it).

theorem_list.name: wifi_stores_only_valid_name
theorem_list.doc: (S) A name is stored only if it is 1 to 32 bytes.

theorem_list.name: pending_save_before_restart
theorem_list.doc: (S) A configuration change answered `204` is saved before any restart.

theorem_list.name: ota_post_only
theorem_list.doc: (S) Only a POST uploads.

theorem_list.name: ota_one_at_a_time
theorem_list.doc: (S) One upload at a time.

theorem_list.name: ota_stream_bounded
theorem_list.doc: (S) An image is streamed only if it is not empty and fits the slot.

theorem_list.name: ota_first_sector_magic
theorem_list.doc: (S) The first sector is written only if it starts with the image magic.

theorem_list.name: ota_restart_only_committed
theorem_list.doc: (S) The device restarts into an upload only if it streamed and committed.

projects.name: AM03127-Controller
properties: Page and schedule ids are valid; encoded messages contain no raw protocol brackets
Message encoding is total; dates and times are two digits
OTA proceeds only with a length and completes exactly when all bytes arrived

theorem_list.name: encode_message_no_raw_brackets
theorem_list.doc: **S (U1 fix).** No byte of the message is copied into the frame as a raw `<` or `>`: every `<` in the encoding starts one of upstream's umlaut tokens `<U..>`, and every `>` ends one. So a message cannot close the frame (`<E>`) or open another command.

theorem_list.name: encode_message_total
theorem_list.doc: **C.** `encode_message` never panics.

theorem_list.name: pages_valid_only_ids
theorem_list.doc: **S (U1 fix).** An accepted schedule page list holds page IDs only.

theorem_list.name: page_id_valid_iff
theorem_list.doc: **C.** Upstream's page-ID check: 'A'..='Z'.

theorem_list.name: schedule_id_valid_iff
theorem_list.doc: **C.** Upstream's schedule-ID check: 'A'..='E'.

theorem_list.name: date_time_two_digits
theorem_list.doc: **S (U2 fix).** An accepted date/time has every field ≤ 99, so each `{:02}` field is two digits and the frame keeps its fixed width.

theorem_list.name: ota_proceeds_only_with_a_length
theorem_list.doc: **S.** The flash is only touched for an octet-stream upload with a declared, non-zero length.

theorem_list.name: ota_complete_iff
theorem_list.doc: **S.** An image counts as complete exactly when every declared byte was written and nothing is left over.

theorem_list.name: waiting_time_letter
theorem_list.doc: **S (U3 fix).** An admitted waiting time prints as 'A'..='Z' (`value + 65 ≤ 90`, no wrap).

projects.name: autodoggo
properties: Overcurrent reverses a closing door and stops an opening one; the timeout stops the motor
A stale overcurrent flag is ignored; no motion is commanded without the driver
A stop is kept while the pulley ramps down
Only one H-bridge channel is driven at a time; duty never exceeds the maximum

theorem_list.name: overcurrent_reverses_closing
theorem_list.doc: (S) An overcurrent while closing reverses the door (it opens).

theorem_list.name: overcurrent_stops_opening
theorem_list.doc: (S) An overcurrent while opening stops the door.

theorem_list.name: timeout_stops
theorem_list.doc: (S) A movement still going at its deadline (10 s after it started) stops: the door goes Idle (and, entering Idle, stops the pulley).

theorem_list.name: stale_overcurrent_ignored
theorem_list.doc: (S) F1: an overcurrent flag already pending when a close starts is taken and discarded: the close goes on (upstream reverses at once).

theorem_list.name: no_motion_without_driver
theorem_list.doc: (S) F2: without the pulley driver, a stopped door stays stopped: no command moves it and it sends the pulley nothing but a stop.

theorem_list.name: stop_kept_while_ramping_down
theorem_list.doc: (S) F3: a stop while ramping down is kept: the pulley stops instead of ramping up the other way.

theorem_list.name: stop_in_hold_cancels
theorem_list.doc: (S) F3: a stop in Hold cancels a pending reversal.

theorem_list.name: one_channel_at_a_time
theorem_list.doc: (S) One channel at a time (the H-bridge's two inputs never both on).

theorem_list.name: duty_at_most_max
theorem_list.doc: (S) No duty over 100 %.

projects.normal_note: All 807 differing scenarios trace to upstream reading the end-stop stall after an ordinary full movement as overcurrent (it then reopens the door). With an end stop that does not read as overcurrent, 250 of 250 scenarios are identical; the effect depends on the door hardware.

projects.name: blind_controller.rs
properties: A move never exceeds the full travel; lowering stops at the bottom
The position estimate follows the moves; idle at the limits
Microstep counts saturate instead of overflowing

theorem_list.name: move_at_most_travel
theorem_list.doc: (S) No command drives more than a full travel.

theorem_list.name: lower_stops_at_bottom
theorem_list.doc: (S) From inside the travel, `Lower` stops at the bottom: it never drives past it (upstream drives a full travel from wherever a jog left the blind).

theorem_list.name: raise_to_top
theorem_list.doc: (S) `Raise` drives up exactly to the top from inside the travel.

theorem_list.name: idle_at_limits
theorem_list.doc: (S) A command at a limit it would drive past does nothing: `Lower` at or past the bottom, `Raise` at the top.

theorem_list.name: microsteps_saturate
theorem_list.doc: (C) The microstep count never wraps (upstream's `n * microsteps` wraps with overflow checks off): the product when it fits, else u32::MAX.

theorem_list.name: estimate_follows
theorem_list.doc: (S) A jog down moves the estimate by the steps driven, at most a full travel, downwards.

theorem_list.name: ramp
theorem_list.doc: (C) The first and last 100 microsteps are slow.

projects.name: garaza-pico-rs
properties: A request starts one pulse of the configured length, which always ends low
Requests during a pulse are coalesced; the next pulse waits for the pause
The relay is high only while a pulse is running

theorem_list.name: request_starts_pulse
theorem_list.doc: (S) A request while idle drives the relay high now, until 500 ms later.

theorem_list.name: pulse_ends_low
theorem_list.doc: (S) The relay is never left high: at the pulse's end it goes low, and the pause (2 s) starts; a waiting request stays waiting.

theorem_list.name: pulse_lasts_its_time
theorem_list.doc: (S) A pulse is never cut short: before its end a timer changes nothing.

theorem_list.name: busy_request_coalesced
theorem_list.doc: (S) Requests during a pulse or its pause are coalesced: the relay is not touched, nothing is armed, one request waits (as upstream's `Signal`).

theorem_list.name: next_pulse_after_pause
theorem_list.doc: (S) After a pause, the next pulse starts only once the pause is over, and only for a waiting request.

theorem_list.name: high_only_starting
theorem_list.doc: (S) The relay goes high only to start a pulse: for a request while idle, or at the end of a pause with a request waiting.

projects.name: omni-wheel-bot
properties: The watchdog stops the motors when commands are overdue and is quiet when disarmed
An active command arms it; a held lease is not taken
The closed control surface needs the secret

theorem_list.name: watchdog_stops_when_overdue
theorem_list.doc: **S.** An armed watchdog whose last active motion command is more than 300 ms old stops the wheels and disarms.

theorem_list.name: watchdog_quiet_when_disarmed
theorem_list.doc: **C.** A disarmed watchdog never stops anything.

theorem_list.name: active_command_arms
theorem_list.doc: **S.** An active motion command arms the watchdog at its time.

theorem_list.name: held_lease_not_taken
theorem_list.doc: **S.** A controller seen within the last 30 s keeps the slot.

theorem_list.name: closed_surface_needs_the_secret
theorem_list.doc: **S.** Unless the surface was explicitly opened, a WebSocket is authorized only with a configured secret that matches.

theorem_list.name: idle_wait_bounds
theorem_list.doc: **C.** The idle wait is 1..=10 ms.

projects.name: energy-monitor-ha
properties: The stored password is never served
Sample-count and period computations never divide by zero
MQTT publishing needs its ids

theorem_list.name: password_never_served
theorem_list.doc: (S) A password is never served: the marker always replaces it.

theorem_list.name: keep_marker
theorem_list.doc: (S) The marker keeps the stored password; anything else replaces it.

theorem_list.name: zero_samples_refused
theorem_list.doc: (S) An STPM config that averages no sample is refused (upstream takes it, and the calibration then divides by zero).

theorem_list.name: no_division_by_zero_samples
theorem_list.doc: (S) No sample with zero readings is calibrated.

theorem_list.name: no_division_by_zero_period
theorem_list.doc: (S) The frequency is computed only from a measured period.

projects.name: aquarium-lid-pcb
properties: Only consistent alarm and fan configurations are admitted
The alarm fires above the high and below the low threshold, is reachable, and clears with hysteresis
The fan turns on above, off below, and holds in between

theorem_list.name: alarm_fires_high
theorem_list.doc: **S (U1).** With an admitted configuration the high alarm sounds at any reading at or above `hi_on`, whatever its state.

theorem_list.name: alarm_fires_low
theorem_list.doc: **S (U1).** … and the low alarm at any reading at or below `lo_on`.

theorem_list.name: alarm_reachable
theorem_list.doc: **S (U1).** Both alarm thresholds lie inside the sensor's range, so there is a reading for each that sounds it (upstream accepts `max_safe_temp = 1000`, which no reading reaches).

theorem_list.name: alarm_clears
theorem_list.doc: **S (U1).** In the quiet band the alarm is off, whatever its state, and an admitted configuration has a quiet band (upstream with `2·h ≥ max − min` keeps it on forever once it fired).

theorem_list.name: alarm_hysteresis
theorem_list.doc: **S.** An admitted configuration has a non-negative hysteresis: the "on" thresholds lie outside the "stay on" thresholds.

theorem_list.name: fan_on_above
theorem_list.doc: **C.** The fan is on at or above `on_at`.

theorem_list.name: fan_off_below
theorem_list.doc: **S.** With an admitted fan configuration it is off at or below `off_at` (no reading is both above `on_at` and below `off_at`).

theorem_list.name: fan_holds_between
theorem_list.doc: **C.** Between the thresholds the fan keeps its state (hysteresis).

projects.name: thermal-printer
properties: Text is only cut at UTF-8 character boundaries and every cut makes progress
Printable output excludes control bytes

theorem_list.name: split_index_progress
theorem_list.doc: **S (U1 fix).** A non-empty line is always cut somewhere in `1..=len` (the loop makes progress; no slicing panic).

theorem_list.name: split_index_boundary
theorem_list.doc: **S (U1 fix).** The cut is a UTF-8 character boundary.

theorem_list.name: chunk_end_progress
theorem_list.doc: **S (U1 fix).** A chunk always advances.

theorem_list.name: printable_excludes_controls
theorem_list.doc: **S (U2 fix).** No C0 control byte (ESC, GS, FS, DLE...) and no DEL is printable.

projects.name: esp-sign
properties: Colour parsing is total and accepts exactly the #rrggbb shape

theorem_list.name: parse_color_total
theorem_list.doc: **S (U1 fix).** Parsing a colour never panics, for any bytes.

theorem_list.name: parse_color_shape
theorem_list.doc: **S.** An accepted colour is 7 bytes with an ASCII first byte.

theorem_list.name: hex_value_digit
theorem_list.doc: **C.** `hex_value` is a digit's value (≤ 15) or 16.

projects.name: esp32-http-stepper
properties: Commands for a motor that does not exist are refused
Zero speed and zero acceleration are refused
Exactly the valid commands are queued

theorem_list.name: no_such_motor
theorem_list.doc: (S) An index past the two motors is refused (upstream: `senders[index]` panics, the device resets).

theorem_list.name: zero_speed_refused
theorem_list.doc: (S) A speed of 0 is refused (upstream: accel-stepper's `set_max_speed(0)` takes `1/0` into a `Duration` and panics).

theorem_list.name: zero_accel_refused
theorem_list.doc: (S) An acceleration of 0 is refused (upstream ignores it: in a motor's first command the driver keeps acceleration 0 and never finishes).

theorem_list.name: valid_command_queued
theorem_list.doc: (S) A valid command reaches the motor it names, unchanged.

theorem_list.name: queued_only_valid
theorem_list.doc: (S) Every command is either valid and queued for the motor it names, or not valid and refused (no such motor, or a bad move): nothing reaches a queue past the two senders, or with a speed or acceleration of 0.

projects.name: chlorophyll
properties: Commands for another device are ignored
An over-long name keeps the old one; an unchanged name is not written
Flash writes are spaced; only valid configurations are stored; over-long datagrams are dropped

theorem_list.name: other_device_ignored
theorem_list.doc: (S) A packet for another device changes nothing.

theorem_list.name: long_name_kept_old
theorem_list.doc: (S) A name over 64 bytes is refused: the stored name stays (upstream stores it empty).

theorem_list.name: unchanged_name_not_written
theorem_list.doc: (S) The name the device already has is announced, never written.

theorem_list.name: writes_spaced
theorem_list.doc: (S) A write happens only when allowed: none since boot, or the last one at least 10 s before (no flash wear by a flood).

theorem_list.name: store_only_valid
theorem_list.doc: (S) A name is stored only when it is for this device, fits, and differs from the stored one.

theorem_list.name: long_datagram_dropped
theorem_list.doc: (S) A datagram over 128 bytes is not decoded (upstream decodes up to 1500 bytes into its 1 KiB heap: a long `SetName` exhausts it, the device resets).

projects.name: cloggo
properties: The linear regression never panics for any calibration data; zero divisors are refused
Pressure conversion never panics
Fixed-point arithmetic is modelled bit-exactly (I32F32)

theorem_list.name: linreg_never_panics
theorem_list.doc: (S) The regression never panics, for any 10 readings: a zero divisor (all readings at one ADC value, or at one pressure) or an overflow is a returned error (upstream: a panic on `GET /linreg`, or wrapped constants).

theorem_list.name: pressure_never_panics
theorem_list.doc: (S) A pressure reading never panics: an overflow is a returned error (upstream wraps).

theorem_list.name: div_by_zero_refused
theorem_list.doc: (S) A zero divisor is an error, never a panic (upstream's `/` panics).

theorem_list.name: mul_total
theorem_list.doc: (C) An `I32F32` product never panics (the exact product fits i128).

theorem_list.name: div_total
theorem_list.doc: (C) An `I32F32` quotient never panics.

projects.name: diy-weather-station
properties: An update starts only with a token and a length that fits
Chunks are contiguous and within the declared length
An update completes iff every byte was written; an aborted update never completes
The new image is confirmed only after the web server is up

theorem_list.name: begin_requires_token_and_fit
theorem_list.doc: **S (U1, U3).** An upload starts only with no upload running, the token, a declared length, and an image that fits the active slot.

theorem_list.name: chunk_within_declared
theorem_list.doc: **S (U2).** A chunk is accepted only within the declared length.

theorem_list.name: chunk_contiguous
theorem_list.doc: **S (U2).** Chunks are written contiguously: each at the bytes written so far, which then grow by its length.

theorem_list.name: complete_iff_all_written
theorem_list.doc: **S.** An image is marked for swap exactly when all its declared bytes were written.

theorem_list.name: abort_never_completes
theorem_list.doc: **S (U3).** An aborted session is never marked.

theorem_list.name: token_ok_needs_configured
theorem_list.doc: **S (U1).** With no token configured (all zero), no request is authorised.

theorem_list.name: confirm_boot_needs_up
theorem_list.doc: **S (U4).** A swapped-in image is confirmed only once the firmware is up.

projects.normal_note: Normal uploads are limited to 1 KiB: larger uploads reach upstream behaviour that differs on every client.

projects.name: pico_dhcp_dns_server
properties: Discovery keeps live leases; a request is acknowledged only for its own lease
DNS answers stay within the packet bounds

theorem_list.name: discover_keeps_live_leases
theorem_list.doc: **S.** A DISCOVER never takes a slot assigned to another client whose lease is still running.

theorem_list.name: request_acks_only_its_own
theorem_list.doc: **S.** A REQUEST is acknowledged only for a slot offered to this client with this transaction, or assigned to it with this transaction and an unexpired lease.

theorem_list.name: answer_fits_bounds
theorem_list.doc: **S (U1 fix).** An answer is written only inside the received question and the buffer.
